findings.impact: D-R21-01 says the table is pinned "so that a re-pinned DRU still cannot drop below it". That holds only for overrides spelled exactly as the generator spells them. Inner PTH hole to copper is backstopped by the board measure (0.3 mm); via hole to inner copper (0.2), outer PTH to track (0.28) and pad hole to hole (0.45) have no board measure, so a reviewed DRU can allow sub-JLC geometry there and the gate stays green. No current board copper is below JLC.
findings.concrete_fix: checks only: in dru_rules() parse every (min V unit) inside each constraint body whatever its position, convert mm / mil / um / in, and treat an unparsable min as a failure; in jlc_hole_table() treat any later rule whose layer is not exactly the pinned word as able to override (any In*.Cu for inner, F.Cu / B.Cu for outer, any named layer for None); add a board-level measure for via hole wall to foreign inner copper (>= 0.2 mm) beside pth_inner_copper. Add the probe cases above as self-test seeds.

findings.impact: The assembly PDFs are bound fab outputs and the hand-fit / rework reference (C84 by hand, fire-path parts). A designator far from its part, a stray wrong designator or an invisible one misleads the rework / inspection reader; JLC placement is from the CPL and is unaffected.
findings.concrete_fix: checks only: in fab_ref_crossings require each reference ink centre inside, or within e.g. 1.5 mm of, its own Fab outline (or courtyard) box; reject any board-level (non-footprint) text on F.Fab / B.Fab; require text thickness >= 0.1 x height (or >= 0.05 mm). The committed board should pass all three (measure before pinning).

findings.impact: D-R20-09 / D-R21-07 hold the clamp beside the pin because ESD effectiveness depends on loop inductance; the clamp-to-GND leg is the other half of that loop and can regress (lose its via) silently. Bounded: the pour still connects it.
findings.concrete_fix: checks only: extend K-ports so each clamp's GND pad reaches a GND via (or GND plated barrel) within a recorded bound (e.g. <= 1.0 mm of track, measured 0.7 mm today) through tracks, not only through the pour.
